correctness.rationale: For arbitrary common-positive job sizes and eligibility at most two, the most recent job assigned to the higher of two pair-specific loads is an EF1 deletion witness, proving the prefixwise online invariant. For unit jobs, bidirectional strong EF1 is equivalent to pair-split imbalance at most one; unit strong EFX coincides. These assignments are exactly orientations of the simple graph of odd pair multiplicities with base loads consisting of forced singles and even half-splits. Necessity and sufficiency of the peak-load inequalities follow from capacities and a capacitated Hall integral matching. The star has exact fair makespan n−1 and unconstrained optimum 2 for n≥3. The accompanying independent enumeration reproduces 3375 exhaustive n=3 parameter profiles, 3500 seeded n=4 profiles and 1200 online streams. These finite checks support but do not replace the analytic proof.

originality.rationale: The October 2026 motivating source proves that strong EF1 can be impossible for larger eligibility hyperedges and gives a three-machine online obstruction using a job eligible for all three. Its examined Sections 5 and Appendix D do not derive the rank-two positive online theorem, the exact unit fair-makespan formula, or the diverging fair-makespan example. The recent graphical-chores primary article examines ordinary envy and equitability, not the pair-restricted strong definition. Classical bounded-orientation feasibility is expressly credited. Actual topical literature and indexed research-record queries returned no covering theorem. This is evidence for best-knowledge originality, not proof of uniqueness.
residual_risks: An unindexed scheduling or fair-orientation paper may already specialize strong EF1 to rank-two eligibility and derive the same formula.
The original 1965 degree-orientation paper was not read in full; its classical characterization is openly credited, so there is no originality assertion about that step.
A related result may use different terms such as pairwise weak envy, eligible-edge balance, or bipartite edge assignment.

value.rationale: The source distinguishes weak from strong envy and proves severe online impossibility in general, making minimal eligibility rank a motivated boundary. A fully general positive strong-EF1 guarantee for every prefix at rank two, a complete explicit unit-allocation classification, an exact peak-load invariant with polynomial-time construction, and an unbounded fairness cost answer substantive existence, characterization, efficiency and computation questions. No general graph orientation theorem is falsely claimed new.
